Part 1 - data exploration, preprocessing & quality control 
1.1 data import and general exploration 
```{r}
# 1.1.1. Load required packages
library(tidyverse)
library(edgeR)

# 1.1.2. Import datasets
counts <- read_csv("GSE80655_counts.csv") %>%
  column_to_rownames("gene_id")
meta <- read_csv("GSE80655_metadata.csv")
meta <- as.data.frame(meta)
rownames(meta) <- meta$description

# 1.1.3. Explore dataset dimensions
dim(counts)
dim(meta)

nrow(counts)   # Number of genes
ncol(counts)   # Number of samples
nrow(meta)     # Number of samples
ncol(meta)     # Number of metadata variables

head(counts[, 1:5])
head(meta)

# 1.1.4. Explore variable names and types
colnames(meta)
str(meta)
str(counts[, 1:5])

head(rownames(counts))
head(colnames(counts))

# 1.1.5. Check duplicated and missing identifiers
sum(duplicated(rownames(counts)))
sum(duplicated(colnames(counts)))
sum(duplicated(meta$description))

sum(is.na(rownames(counts)))
sum(is.na(colnames(counts)))
sum(is.na(meta$description))

# 1.1.6. Check sample alignment
# Check whether both datasets contain the same samples
setequal(colnames(counts), meta$description)
setdiff(colnames(counts), meta$description)
setdiff(meta$description, colnames(counts))

stopifnot(setequal(colnames(counts), meta$description))

# Check whether samples are in the same order

all(colnames(counts) == meta$description)

# Reorder counts according to metadata

counts <- counts[, meta$description]

stopifnot(all(colnames(counts) == meta$description))

dim(counts)
```

1.2 metadata exploration and preprocessing
```{r}
# 1.2.1. Explore numerical variables
summary(meta$age)
summary(meta$PMI)
summary(meta$brain_pH)

sd(meta$age, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(meta$PMI, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(meta$brain_pH, na.rm = TRUE)

# Explore categorical variables
table(meta$diagnosis)
table(meta$brain_region)
table(meta$sex)
table(meta$ethnicity)

# Calculate percentages
prop.table(table(meta$diagnosis)) * 100
prop.table(table(meta$brain_region)) * 100
prop.table(table(meta$sex)) * 100
prop.table(table(meta$ethnicity)) * 100

# 1.2.2. Identification of missing values
# Number of missing values per variable
colSums(is.na(meta))

# Percentage of missing values per variable
colMeans(is.na(meta)) * 100

# Investigate samples with missing brain pH
meta %>%
  filter(is.na(brain_pH))

# Identify donors with missing brain pH
meta %>%
  filter(is.na(brain_pH)) %>%
  distinct(donor_id)

# No samples or donors are removed at this stage.

# 1.2.3. Samples versus donors
# Total number of tissue samples
nrow(meta)

# Number of unique donors
n_distinct(meta$donor_id)

# Number of samples contributed by each donor
table(meta$donor_id)

# Distribution of the number of samples per donor
table(table(meta$donor_id))

# 1.2.4. Check consistency within donors
# Investigate whether donor-level variables differ
# between samples originating from the same donor.
donor_check <- meta %>%
  group_by(donor_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_age = n_distinct(age),
    n_sex = n_distinct(sex),
    n_diagnosis = n_distinct(diagnosis),
    n_ethnicity = n_distinct(ethnicity),
    n_PMI = n_distinct(PMI),
    n_pH = n_distinct(brain_pH),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(if_any(starts_with("n_"), ~ .x > 1))

donor_check

# Investigate any inconsistencies before donor-level analyses.
# Do not remove or aggregate samples yet.

# 1.2.5. Convert categorical variables into factors
meta <- meta %>%
  mutate(
    diagnosis = as.factor(diagnosis),
    brain_region = as.factor(brain_region),
    sex = as.factor(sex),
    ethnicity = as.factor(ethnicity),
    donor_id = as.factor(donor_id)
  )

str(meta)

# 1.2.6. Visualization of metadata distributions
# Age distribution
ggplot(meta, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 20,
    fill = "steelblue",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of age",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Number of samples"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# PMI distribution
ggplot(meta, aes(x = PMI)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 20,
    fill = "steelblue",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of post-mortem interval",
    x = "PMI (hours)",
    y = "Number of samples"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Brain pH distribution
ggplot(meta, aes(x = brain_pH)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 20,
    fill = "steelblue",
    color = "white",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of brain pH",
    x = "Brain pH",
    y = "Number of samples"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Distribution of psychiatric diagnoses
ggplot(meta, aes(x = diagnosis, fill = diagnosis)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of psychiatric diagnoses",
    x = "Diagnosis",
    y = "Number of samples"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )


# Distribution of brain regions
ggplot(meta, aes(x = brain_region, fill = brain_region)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of brain regions",
    x = "Brain region",
    y = "Number of samples"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")


# Distribution of sex
ggplot(meta, aes(x = sex, fill = sex)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of sex",
    x = "Sex",
    y = "Number of samples"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")


# Distribution of ethnicity
ggplot(meta, aes(x = ethnicity, fill = ethnicity)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of ethnicity",
    x = "Ethnicity",
    y = "Number of samples"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

# These visualizations are sample-level descriptions.
# Repeated samples from the same donor are included.

# 1.2.7. Identification of potential outliers
# Boxplots of numerical variables
boxplot(
  meta$age,
  main = "Age",
  ylab = "Age (years)",
  col = "lightblue"
)

boxplot(
  meta$PMI,
  main = "Post-mortem interval",
  ylab = "PMI (hours)",
  col = "lightblue"
)

boxplot(
  meta$brain_pH,
  main = "Brain pH",
  ylab = "Brain pH",
  col = "lightblue"
)

# Identify potential outlier values using the IQR method
boxplot.stats(meta$age)$out
boxplot.stats(meta$PMI)$out
boxplot.stats(meta$brain_pH)$out

# Potential outliers are investigated, not automatically removed.

# 1.2.8. Summary of metadata preprocessing
dim(meta)
n_distinct(meta$donor_id)
colSums(is.na(meta))

# All samples and donors are retained.
# Analysis-specific preprocessing will be performed in Part 2.
```
1.3 Raw RNA-seq data exploration 

```{r}
# 1.3.1. Check missing and invalid values
# Check whether all count columns are numeric
all(vapply(counts, is.numeric, logical(1)))

# Convert counts to a numeric matrix
count_matrix <- as.matrix(counts)

# Check missing values
sum(is.na(count_matrix))

# Check negative values
sum(count_matrix < 0, na.rm = TRUE)

# Check infinite values
sum(is.infinite(count_matrix))

# Check non-integer values
sum(count_matrix %% 1 != 0, na.rm = TRUE)

# Verify data integrity before proceeding
stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(count_matrix)),
  all(count_matrix >= 0),
  all(count_matrix %% 1 == 0)
)

# 1.3.2. Investigation of zero counts
# Total number of expression values
length(count_matrix)

# Total number of zero counts
sum(count_matrix == 0)

# Percentage of zero counts
mean(count_matrix == 0) * 100

# Genes with zero counts across all samples
sum(rowSums(count_matrix == 0) == ncol(count_matrix))

# Percentage of completely unexpressed genes
mean(rowSums(count_matrix == 0) == ncol(count_matrix)) * 100

# Number of zero counts per sample
zero_counts_per_sample <- colSums(count_matrix == 0)
summary(zero_counts_per_sample)

# Zero counts are not missing values.

# 1.3.3. Library size exploration

# Calculate total counts per sample
library_sizes <- colSums(count_matrix)
summary(library_sizes)

# Check for empty libraries
stopifnot(all(library_sizes > 0))

# Create a dataframe for visualization
library_df <- data.frame(
  sample = colnames(counts),
  library_size = library_sizes
)

# Histogram of library sizes
ggplot(library_df, aes(x = library_size)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 30,
    fill = "steelblue",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of library sizes",
    x = "Total counts per sample",
    y = "Number of samples"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Boxplot of library sizes
ggplot(library_df, aes(y = library_size)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Library size variation",
    y = "Total counts per sample"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# 1.3.4. Raw gene expression distributions
# Histogram of raw expression values
hist(
  log2(count_matrix + 1),
  breaks = 50,
  col = "steelblue",
  main = "Distribution of raw gene expression",
  xlab = "Log2(raw counts + 1)",
  ylab = "Frequency"
)

# Boxplots of raw counts for the first five samples
counts[, 1:5] %>%
  rownames_to_column("gene_id") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = !gene_id) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = name, y = log10(value + 1))) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Raw gene expression distributions",
    x = "Sample",
    y = "Log10(raw counts + 1)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Log transformation is used here for visualization only.
```
1.4 RNA-SEQ preprocessing

```{r}
# 1.4.1. Create DGEList and calculate CPM
# Create an edgeR DGEList object
dge <- DGEList(
  counts = count_matrix,
  group = meta$diagnosis
)

dim(dge)

# Calculate counts per million (CPM)
cpm_values <- cpm(dge)
dim(cpm_values)

# Inspect CPM values
cpm_values[1:6, 1:6]


# 1.4.2. Low-expression filtering
# Retain genes with CPM >= 1 in at least 10% of samples
min_samples <- ceiling(0.10 * ncol(dge))
min_samples

# Identify genes meeting the filtering criterion
keep <- rowSums(cpm_values >= 1) >= min_samples

# Number of retained and removed genes
table(keep)

# Filter the original raw counts
# Recalculate library sizes after filtering
dge <- dge[keep, , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE]

# Store filtered raw counts separately
counts_filtered <- dge$counts
dim(counts_filtered)


# 1.4.3. Check dimensions after filtering
# Dimensions before filtering
dim(counts)

# Dimensions after filtering
dim(dge)

# Number of retained genes
nrow(dge)

# Number of removed genes
nrow(counts) - nrow(dge)

# Percentage of retained genes
nrow(dge) / nrow(counts) * 100

# Percentage of removed genes
(1 - nrow(dge) / nrow(counts)) * 100

# Verify that no samples were removed
stopifnot(ncol(dge) == ncol(counts))

# Visualize retained and removed genes
filter_df <- data.frame(
  Status = c("Retained", "Removed"),
  Genes = c(
    nrow(dge),
    nrow(counts) - nrow(dge)
  )
)

ggplot(filter_df, aes(x = Status, y = Genes, fill = Status)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = Genes), vjust = -0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Gene retention after low-expression filtering",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of genes"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")


# 1.4.4. TMM normalization
# Calculate TMM normalization factors
dge <- calcNormFactors(dge, method = "TMM")

# Inspect sample information
head(dge$samples)

# Summary of normalization factors
summary(dge$samples$norm.factors)

# Calculate effective library sizes
effective_library_sizes <-
  dge$samples$lib.size * dge$samples$norm.factors

summary(effective_library_sizes)

# Calculate TMM-normalized CPM values
cpm_matrix <- cpm(dge)
dim(cpm_matrix)
cpm_matrix[1:6, 1:6]

# Compare raw counts and normalized CPM for ACTB

if ("ENSG00000075624" %in% rownames(dge$counts)) {
  plot(
    dge$counts["ENSG00000075624", ],
    cpm_matrix["ENSG00000075624", ],
    xlab = "Raw counts",
    ylab = "Normalized CPM",
    main = "ACTB: raw counts versus normalized CPM"
  )
}

# 1.4.5. Log2-CPM transformation
# Calculate TMM-normalized log2-CPM values
# A prior count is used to handle zero counts.

logcpm <- cpm(
  dge,
  log = TRUE,
  prior.count = 2
)

dim(logcpm)

logcpm[1:6, 1:6]
```
1.5 Quality control after reproccesing

```{r}

# 1.5.1. Comparison before and after TMM normalization
# Calculate CPM without TMM normalization factors
cpm_before <- cpm(
  dge,
  normalized.lib.sizes = FALSE
)

# Calculate CPM with TMM normalization factors
cpm_after <- cpm(
  dge,
  normalized.lib.sizes = TRUE
)
# Both matrices contain the same genes and samples.

# Boxplots before TMM normalization

as.data.frame(cpm_before)[, 1:5] %>%
  rownames_to_column("gene_id") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = !gene_id) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = name, y = log2(value + 1))) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Before TMM normalization",
    x = "Sample",
    y = "Log2(CPM + 1)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Boxplots after TMM normalization

as.data.frame(cpm_after)[, 1:5] %>%
  rownames_to_column("gene_id") %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = !gene_id) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = name, y = log2(value + 1))) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightgreen") +
  labs(
    title = "After TMM normalization",
    x = "Sample",
    y = "Log2(CPM + 1)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Compare all samples before and after normalization
boxplot(
  log2(cpm_before + 1),
  outline = FALSE,
  xaxt = "n",
  col = "lightblue",
  main = "All samples before TMM normalization",
  xlab = "Samples",
  ylab = "Log2(CPM + 1)"
)

boxplot(
  log2(cpm_after + 1),
  outline = FALSE,
  xaxt = "n",
  col = "lightgreen",
  main = "All samples after TMM normalization",
  xlab = "Samples",
  ylab = "Log2(CPM + 1)"
)


# 1.5.2. Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
# Transpose the expression matrix:
# Rows = samples
# Columns = genes
pca <- prcomp(
  t(logcpm),
  center = TRUE,
  scale. = FALSE
)

# Calculate explained variance
variance_explained <-
  pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2) * 100

# Explained variance of the first ten PCs
variance_explained[1:10]

# Cumulative explained variance
cumsum(variance_explained)[1:10]


# Scree plot
variance_df <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:10,
  Variance = variance_explained[1:10]
)

ggplot(variance_df, aes(x = PC, y = Variance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(
    title = "Explained variance per principal component",
    x = "Principal component",
    y = "Explained variance (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# 1.5.3. Investigation of sources of variation
# Extract PCA coordinates
pca_df <- as.data.frame(pca$x)

# Verify sample alignment
stopifnot(all(rownames(pca_df) == rownames(meta)))

# Add metadata to PCA coordinates
pca_df <- cbind(pca_df, meta)

# Create axis labels with explained variance
pc1_label <- paste0(
  "PC1 (", round(variance_explained[1], 1), "%)"
)
pc2_label <- paste0(
  "PC2 (", round(variance_explained[2], 1), "%)"
)

# PCA coloured by brain region
ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, color = brain_region)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA by brain region",
    x = pc1_label,
    y = pc2_label,
    color = "Brain region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# PCA coloured by psychiatric diagnosis
ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, color = diagnosis)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA by psychiatric diagnosis",
    x = pc1_label,
    y = pc2_label,
    color = "Diagnosis"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# PCA coloured by sex
ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, color = sex)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA by sex",
    x = pc1_label,
    y = pc2_label,
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# PCA coloured by age
ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, color = age)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    title = "PCA by age",
    x = pc1_label,
    y = pc2_label,
    color = "Age"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# PCA coloured by brain pH
ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, color = brain_pH)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(na.value = "grey70") +
  labs(
    title = "PCA by brain pH",
    x = pc1_label,
    y = pc2_label,
    color = "Brain pH"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# PCA coloured by post-mortem interval
ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, color = PMI)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    title = "PCA by post-mortem interval",
    x = pc1_label,
    y = pc2_label,
    color = "PMI"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# PCA coloured by ethnicity
ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, color = ethnicity)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA by ethnicity",
    x = pc1_label,
    y = pc2_label,
    color = "Ethnicity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# PCA coloured by original library size
pca_df$library_size <- library_sizes[
  match(rownames(pca_df), names(library_sizes))
]

ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, color = library_size)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    title = "PCA by library size",
    x = pc1_label,
    y = pc2_label,
    color = "Library size"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# 1.5.4. Identification of potential outliers
# PCA with sample identifiers
ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = description),
    check_overlap = TRUE,
    size = 2.5
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA for potential outlier detection",
    x = pc1_label,
    y = pc2_label
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Potential outliers require further investigation.
# No samples are automatically removed based on PCA.

# 1.5.5. Summary of preprocessing
# Original raw count matrix
dim(counts)

# Filtered raw count matrix
dim(counts_filtered)

# Normalized CPM matrix
dim(cpm_matrix)

# Normalized log2-CPM matrix
dim(logcpm)

# Metadata
dim(meta)

# Number of unique donors
n_distinct(meta$donor_id)

# Final sample alignment
stopifnot(all(colnames(logcpm) == rownames(meta)))

# Create a summary table
preprocessing_summary <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c(
    "Number of genes",
    "Number of samples",
    "Number of unique donors",
    "Low-expression filtering",
    "TMM normalization",
    "Log2-CPM transformation"
  ),
  Before = c(
    nrow(counts),
    ncol(counts),
    n_distinct(meta$donor_id),
    "No",
    "No",
    "No"
  ),
  After = c(
    nrow(logcpm),
    ncol(logcpm),
    n_distinct(meta$donor_id),
    "Yes",
    "Yes",
    "Yes"
  )
)

preprocessing_summary

# Display summary table in R Markdown

knitr::kable(
  preprocessing_summary,
  caption = "Summary of RNA-seq data preprocessing"
)
```
